claim: The 1980s bouillabaisse charter requires only locally caught rockfish and sets strict criteria for the accompanying bread and rouille sauce.
quote: Established in the 1980s, the bouillabaisse charter ensures quality standards. Requirements include using only locally caught rockfish and establishing strict criteria for accompanying bread and sauce.

claim: Chez Fonfon in the Vallon des Auffes fishing port serves a traditional bouillabaisse made with five different fish from local fishermen.
quote: Located in the Auffes valley fishing port, this institution relies on local fishermen. Their bouillabaisse is traditional and made with five different fish. It's a perfect combination of freshness and authenticity!

claim: L'Épuisette, run by chef Guillaume Sourrieu, serves a refined bouillabaisse with a view over the harbour and Frioul Islands.
quote: Chef Guillaume Sourrieu's refined version features a stunning view overlooking the harbor and Frioul Islands as part of an inventive menu.

claim: Chez Fonfon sits in the small fishing port of Vallon des Auffes below the Corniche Kennedy and serves bouillabaisse as a starter soup or shareable main.
quote: An institution of the small fishing port of the valley of Auffes, below the Corniche Kennedy, Chez Fonfon has always relied on the fishermen of the valley to fill its kitchen with the goods of the sea.

claim: Le Miramar on the Vieux-Port is a founding member of the bouillabaisse charter; its chef Christian Buffa is a Maître Cuisinier de France.
quote: Christian Buffa - founding member and vice-president of the Bouillabaisse Charter - is also a Maître Cuisinier de France and Maître Restaurateur.

claim: Le Four des Navettes, at 136 rue Sainte by the Abbaye Saint-Victor, is Marseille's oldest bakery, operating since 1781 with a secret navette recipe.
quote: Tradition marseillaise depuis 1781 ... 136, rue Sainte (Saint-Victor) 13007 Marseille ... Le secret le mieux gardé de Marseille

claim: Navettes are orange-blossom-flavoured boat-shaped cookies created in 1781, eaten at Chandeleur and said to commemorate the boat that brought the Marys to Provence.
quote: Created in 1781, the navettes de Marseille are cookies flavored with orange blossom, often enjoyed at Chandeleur. The boat shape is said to commemorate Mary Magdalene and Saint Martha and their boat trip to Marseille 2,000 years ago.

claim: Panisse, chickpea-flour fritters originating in Marseille's l'Estaque district from 1930s Italian workers, are gluten-free, vegan, and sold by the dozen in paper wraps as street food.
quote: Panisse is a type of chickpea flour pancakes originating from Marseille's l'Estaque district. It's believed that Italian workers brought their chickpea bread into the region back in the 1930s. Gluten-free and vegan ... usually sold by dozens in small paper wraps in the streets

claim: Pastis, a strong cold-served anise spirit, is the emblematic aperitif drink of Marseille.
quote: Pastis is a must-have at aperitifs in Marseille. This strong and fragrant anise, served very cold, is the emblematic drink of the city.

claim: Marché des Capucins in the Noailles district has ~20 stalls plus surrounding shops, mainly North African, open Monday-Saturday mornings near Métro Noailles.
quote: From Monday to Saturday morning, around 20 stalls and all surrounding shops prepare their goods, mainly representing North African cultures.

claim: Noailles, nicknamed the 'belly of Marseille,' is a multicultural quarter of North African shops, spices, halal butchers, bakeries and street food.
quote: It's a true reflection of the multicultural aspects of Marseille, all together in 1 vibrant and lively marketplace. Visitors love the nearby African restaurants, bakeries, and shops offering traditional goodies.

claim: Cha'Houla, a Comorian restaurant at 65 boulevard Jeanne d'Arc, serves samboussas, mabawas and customisable Comobowls reflecting Marseille's large Comorian community.
quote: A Comorian restaurant offering Comobowls personalizables, signature Comobowls, and traditional snacks including samboussas and mabawas. Located at 65 boulevard Jeanne d'Arc, 13005 Marseille

claim: Douceur Piquante, a Comorian eatery at 11bis rue Guy Môquet beside Lycée Thiers in Noailles, serves home-style recipes by chef Nadjatie Bacar.
quote: Located next to Lycée Thiers in the Noailles neighborhood of Marseille. Nadjatie Bacar offers a variety of recipes where she adds a twist using local ingredients. The restaurant is at 11bis Rue Guy Môquet 13001 Marseille

claim: Cours Julien is Marseille's bohemian dining hub; budget meals run roughly EUR 10-18 and many panisse and street-food vendors are cash-only.
quote: Budget approximately EUR10-EUR18 for casual meals and EUR30-EUR55 for a proper bistro dinner. Some of the best panisse and street food vendors are cash-only, so it's wise to bring cash

claim: Bistro du Cours at 13 Cours Julien is a value bistro offering a three-course lunch around EUR 20.
quote: Bistro du Cours stands out as an excellent value option. It offers lunch options from 16 to 32 Euros, with a 20 Euro three-course meal that represents a true bargain.
